summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (no commentary; reference only)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE EMBLEMS OF FIDELITY (James Lane Allen, 1919, Doubleday, Page; a comedy in letters)
Epigraph: Chesterfield, "There is nothing so ill-bred as audible laughter."
Dedication: "To the Spirit of Comedy, Incomparable Ally of Victory."

**Characters:** Edward Blackthorne (famous elderly English novelist, King Alfred's Wood, Warwickshire); Beverley Sands (rising young American novelist, Cathedral Heights, NY, Kentucky novels, age 27); Benjamin "Ben" Doolittle (practical lawyer, 150 Broad St / later 150 Wall St; "land-turtle"; signs "Ben (alias Sal Blivvens)"); George Marigold (fashionable physician, Dr. G. M.); Claude Mullen (fashionable nerve specialist, friend of Marigold; "giraffe-headed jackass"); Rufus Kent (long-winded president of The Great Dipper club, "Nestor"); Noah Chamberlain (absent-minded botany professor, Seminole NC, "Approximations to Consciousness in Plants"; Litt.D.); Clara Louise Chamberlain (his daughter, secretary, "proud daughter of the Southland"); Phillips & Faulds, Burns & Bruce, Judd & Judd, Andy Peters (florists); Hodge (Blackthorne's stupid gardener; Latin plant names; "Bishop's crooks" fern shoots); Tilly Snowden (Beverley's fiancée; "Slippery Elm" Apartments; wild rose in snow bank); Polly Boles (Ben's sweetheart; Franklin Flats; "Tilly's friend"); Anne Raeburn (Blackthorne's secretary); Mrs. Blackthorne.

**Chronology & events:**
- May 1, 1910: Blackthorne writes Sands admiring his Kentucky novel; asks for Kentucky ferns for his fern bank (Corot/Turgenieff/Nilsson story; Turgenieff said "Ferns were growing thereabouts"; a hamper of Russian fern-roots came with Turgenieff's card). Offers pounds sterling; budget ~£5.
- May 12: Sands replies, shipment to be arranged; mails catalogues. Notes "Mrs. Sands" unknown.
- May 22: Blackthorne's Hodge comedy (Latin names, "Asplenium filix-faemina", "Bishop's crooks"; Hodge's "personal promontory"); invites Sands and wife; "proboscis" metaphor.
- June 3: Sands to Tilly: jokes about Blackthorne invitation, Stonehenge tea, "foreign exchange." Tilly (June 4) replies: "Canaan and his strip" (her mother's friend, minister's wife); she is a patient of Dr. Marigold; she plans "Bulgar bacillus"; postponed marriage repeatedly.
- June 3: Sands to Ben re ferns; Ben's reply June 5 ("land-turtle", "polecat of the human faculties", "A chaque oiseau son nid est beau"); Ben refers to Phillips & Faulds.
- June 6–7: Polly/Ben/Tilly letters; Tilly's rant on "Not Necessarily Monogamous!" banner; Polly: "the domestic tea-kettle... overdoing the stove."
- June 7, 1900 (sic): Sands orders ferns from Phillips & Faulds ($25 check); June 10 P&F accept.
- June 15: Sands to Blackthorne: "peach and bough" image; wife "unwed"; Sands' postscript on shadows/penumbra.
- June 16 Diary: Sands' fake "woodland scene with ferns"—real memory: dry spring, sycamore, August afternoon at age 17; "There was no woodland scene and there were no ferns."
- PART SECOND. May 1, 1911: Blackthorne's angry letter: ferns never arrived; "Fern stood for Fidelity"; "crystallisation"; cabbage/oak/plover metaphors.
- May 10, 1911: Sands' terse reply ("I have never felt called upon to defend my character").
- Sands to Ben May 13 (enclosing letters); Phillips & Faulds May 13 blame Burns & Bruce, senior member ill, litigation.
- Burns & Bruce (Dunkirk, Tenn.) May 20: blame drought/frost, and Phillips & Faulds' debts; recommend Noah Chamberlain (Seminole NC).
- Sands to Chamberlain May 25 with $25 check. Noah Chamberlain May 29: "I am not a florist," professor of botany; daughter Clara returns check. Clara's indignant letter ("People of our means...do not peddle bulbs"). Sands June 3 apology ("A.B. (merely)"). Noah June 8: "Stop writing to me." Clara June 8: father's distress ("Think of his calling me a famous liar!").
- June 12: Sands to Ben re Tilly; decides not to tell Tilly about ferns; Ben June 13 advises (rock; "closets").
- June 15: Tilly breaks engagement (wants to go to England as ordinary tourists); Polly's appointment; Ben and Polly jointly sign note (June 15) "POLLY BOLES AND BENJAMIN DOOLITTLE" to Sands ("the love devil").
- Tilly's letters to Dr. Marigold (June 17–21): bills; Kentucky horse; her childhood (six sisters; father/mother suffrage fight; living pets vs. dolls; "long love is possible only when you love often"); she sails-away letter to Marigold ("Venus of the deep"; mentions Marigold planning to visit Blackthorne in England).
- June 21: Tilly to Sands ("For I love you"); Tilly to Polly (hates her; "Ask Ben... Or shall I?").
- June 23–28: Polly's worries about Dr. Mullen; Ben's advice ("institution for the weak-minded"; "furnace-man" joke).
- July 14–15: Ben's "I. s. y. s. r. r." note; Polly: Mullen no longer bothers her.
- July 16–23: Sands orders Kentucky ferns via Judd & Judd ($25 + extra). Clara sends list (father died; mislaid list).
- Dec 27 1911 (lettering): Judd & Judd: ferns returned, charges. Sands pays $50 (Dec 30). Dec 28: "The ferns have have come back to me from England!"
- Dec 25 (1911): Clara's letter: father died after falling down stairs (candle, lumbago, pneumonia) while worrying over the fern list.
- Jan 7 (1912): Clara asks for ferns orders to go to Andy Peters' florist (Seminole).
- Jan 10–11: Sands/Ben on Clara; Ben's "Southland" satire.
- Rufus Kent (Jan 12, Great Dipper club): explains club gossip; Blackthorne's hostility from tourists' visit (Sands' name; "That was once reserved for some ferns"). Kent invites Sands to dinner.
- Part Third: Clara's letters May 1912 (Andy Peters' greenhouse; asks Sands to inscribe his novel "For Miss Clara Louise Chamberlain"); Sands sends cheque; Clara: "Mr. Andy Peters has begun to offer me his attentions"; wants NY secretary job; "Mr Andy Peters is a confirmed rascal."
- May 24, 1912: Sands to Ben: "Clara Louise Chamberlain is in New York! God Almighty!"; Ben May 25 writes to Clara (DOOLITTLE hires her under pretext); Ben's May 27 mock "adventuress" dictation (fine $25, "pay a few tears of penitence"); Clara disappears. Sands May 28 scolds; Ben May 29 apology.
- May 30: Tilly to Polly (suspects Beverley's mental state, ferns episode in her parlor: flowers with ferns; Beverley muttering to the ferns). Polly June 2: mother ill in Louisville. Tilly's second letter: Dr. Marigold & Dr. Mullen questions.
- June 4: Ben to Phillips & Faulds (roses to Polly). June 4–5: Ben to Polly; June 5 Ben reports to Polly on "dictograph" plot: they recorded Beverley's raving about Marigold & Mullen; uproar at meeting with two doctors, Club president and two Club "gossips," Beverley sent to Brooklyn.
- June 10, 1912: Ben to Edward Blackthorne (150 Wall St): "Johnson's Richard the Third", "cocksure" analysis, "Sal Blivvens."
- June 21: Blackthorne's reply (Sal Blivvens, "Ned and Sal Blivvens", Tommy's pudding; cocksures; Burns "Then gently scan your brother man / To step aside is human"); Blackthorne apologises, invites Sands, "Will you, after all, send the ferns?"
- June 30: Ben's note (Blackthorne made him "Sal Blivvens"; ferns won't be Blackthorne's).
- July 1: Sands; Blackthorne's second letter (announces Hodge is dead; "two oak trees reach one another with their branches").
- July 4–12: Phillips & Faulds, Burns & Bruce, Andy Peters (seedlins) pitch new business; Ben July 7 announces Tilly's marriage to Dr. Marigold and Polly coming "with her wedding clothes."
- July 8: Sands: "I traced Miss Chamberlain... royalties are human gratitude."
- Meditation in verse ("Polly comes with the wedding clothes").
- July 10: Ben: Polly arrived NY, disappeared. Sands met Polly (wedding clothes, "You will hear").
- July 11: Polly Boles married Dr. Claude Mullen at City Hall, Jersey City.
- July 18 Diary: Tilly's wedding day; Sands' last meeting with Tilly ("Lift my veil... Kiss me"); Ocean Grove honeymoon; Sands sails to England; "emblems of fidelity."

## BOOK 2 of 2: SKINNY McCORD (Percy Keese Fitzhugh, 1928, Grosset & Dunlap; illus. Howard L. Hastings; Temple Camp series)
Frontispiece: "He groped blindly for the projecting tree."

**Characters:** Skinny McCord (Alfred McCord; Bridgeboro NJ scout, Elk Patrol, Connie Bennett's patrol; sensitive, bashful; 64 pounds; second summer at Temple Camp; mascot, "Shorty", "Tiny", "Alf"); Danny McCord (half-brother, 16, escaped Blythedale Boys' Home reform school; gray eyes; tattoo "D.M." on arm; "Danville Bently" impostor); Roy Blakeley (Silver Foxes; "jolliers"); Pee-wee Harris (mentioned); Tom Slade (camp assistant); Uncle Jeb (Rushmore; trapper); Brent Gaylong; Councilor Barrows; Councilor Wainwright (Wainey, camp authority); Councilor Tenny; Mr. Ellsworth (scoutmaster, Bridgeboro troop); Connie Bennett (Elk patrol leader); Vic Norris; Stut Moran; Bert McAlpin; Hunt Ward; Kinney (Irontown, knocked out by Danny); Helmer Clarkson (rich Elk-ish boy with grapefruit & figs); Holman Sharpe (New Hampshire pioneer scout; "Sharpy"); Ralph Warner; Warde Hollister; Howell Cross (Vermont Eagle); Ellis Carway (Eagle); Holly Hollis (Eagle from Bridgeboro); Chocolate Drop (cook); Charlie Avery; Pompy Arliss; Mary Temple (cup); John Temple (founder); Doc Carson; Councilor Wallace; Mr. Burt (Ford); Dick Kinney; Vic Norris' patrol "Alligators of Alleghany"; Bert Winton; Collie Edwards (bird house).

**Chronology & events:**
- Ch. I: Camp-fire at Temple Camp (Black Lake, Greene Co., NY). Skinny loses small tin compass; scouts tease him.
- Ch. II: Stranger (Danny) on bench at road sign "To Temple Camp"; finds unopened letter from Roswell T. Bently, Wave Crest City, Florida (June 27, 1927) to Board of Councilors: son Danville Bently delayed from July to August 2 (trip to Europe).
- Ch. III: Danny's escape story (Blythedale; grape-vine; ice-tongs; 51 miles). Pennant cabin confrontation.
- Ch. IV–V: Danny and Skinny meet at dead camp-fire; Danny's plan. Skinny's hideout: old switchman's shanty with red lantern in railroad cut. Skinny gave away $11 (bought scout suit in Kingston with money from father's $15).
- Ch. VI–VIII: Danny plans impersonation of Danville Bently. Skinny steals white pennant from Alligators of Alleghany cabin (barefoot, shoes around neck).
- Ch. IX–X: Skinny swims across Black Lake for Hiawatha Prize canoe; collapses on shore; fisherman rescues; Councilor Wallace/launch.
- Ch. XI–XII: Skinny tries to sell canoe to Helmer Clarkson for $15 (fails: Clarkson leaving camp). Danny (as "Danville Bently") registers at Administration Shack.
- Ch. XIII–XIV: Skinny exposed; Vic Norris insults him; Danny punches Vic ("Do you take that back?"). Danny at Pioneer Row; Holman Sharpe.
- Ch. XV–XVII: Holman's fight with Ralph Warner; Danny takes blame; expelled by Councilor Wainwright; $70; returns $70 in envelope "To the Managers of Temple Camp."
- Ch. XVIII–XIX: Danny leaves via 6:32 train (Holman's fault unresolved). Real Danville Bently arrives Aug 2 with white scarf (Polar Bears of Florida), silver ring.
- Ch. XX–XXII: Bulletin notice about impersonator; Danville befriends Skinny; wins canoe-tipping trick; Test Four plans; "Sunday School boys" joke.
- Ch. XXIII–XXVI: Henny's Cave (seven-mile hike). Danville and Skinny enter; smoke fills cave; Danville saves someone; Skinny opens air shaft with long stick; rattlesnake coils around Skinny's leg.
- Ch. XXVII–XXVIII: Danville kills snake with jack-knife, pins to bark; rescued person is Danny (not a stranger, as Danville thought); Danny confesses; Danville refuses Gold Cross ("I'm a stingy scout").
- Ch. XXIX–XXX: Danny's postcard from Porto Rico ($10); Skinny sold out by Elks (Holly Hollis, Eagle, replaces him); Danville rents Overlook Cabin on Black Hill for $12/week; Danville tells Elks (Connie).
- Ch. XXXI–XXXII: Overlook Cabin described (signal easel; marsh; frogs); night before Mary Temple Cup race: Howell Cross, Ellis Carway, Holly Hollis.
- Ch. XXXIII: Race; Hollis capsizes into marsh; Skinny tears down signal easel (canvas) to float over marsh, rescues Hollis.
- Ch. XXXIV: Holly Hollis resigns from Elk patrol to join Danville's patrol; Danville: "An Eagle is not as high as you can go." ("The Gold Cross" theme; "Elk Patrol" loses Eagle.)

Key quoted phrases: "Canaan and his strip"; "Fidelity"; "Le Génie Oblige"; "Not Necessarily Monogamous!"; "Bishop's crooks"; "I. s. y. s. r. r."; "An Eagle is not as high as you can go."
